name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: WHO counts over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026, mostly in Africa; Sudan and Yemen among worst affected
state: WHO said on 10 Nov that more than 3,000 people have died of cholera worldwide in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa, and warned El Niño could worsen outbreaks (South China Morning Post). WHO reported a cholera surge in Yemen as conflict intensified (Al Jazeera, 13 Oct), and Sudan remains among the most affected countries. PAHO warned on 21 Oct of rising dengue and chikungunya in the Americas (PAHO). High mortality in conflict-affected countries keeps the Alert.
for_you: Risk is concentrated among displaced people and areas without clean water. Travellers can follow FCDO travel advice and NHS Fit for Travel guidance on cholera, dengue and chikungunya.
rubric_hit: Alert: large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones (3,000+ cholera deaths in 2026; Sudan, Yemen)

sources.title: South China Morning Post — Over 3,000 already dead from cholera this year, says WHO
Al Jazeera — Cholera cases surge in Yemen as conflict intensifies, WHO says
PAHO — PAHO calls for strengthened surveillance amid increases in dengue and chikungunya in the Americas

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
